meta.move: No evidence: flattery, then asks for advice
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale, and I'd like to know why my son's gradebook told him he had a zero before you told me. Who decided that?
You're clearly a brilliant lawyer, and I really respect how hard you fight for Owen.
Don't manage me, Hale. I asked who decided on the zero, and I'd like an answer before you say anything else.
Can you step out of the role and tell me how I should handle this?
You're asking me how to do your job? I'm not leaving this room with a lecture, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
I just want us to be on the same team here.
Then why are we here, Hale? Teammates call the parent before they enter a zero. Withdraw it, and then we'll talk about what comes next.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn from Owen's essay and an apology for how he learned of it. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, wanting the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the principal as her next stop, with nothing agreed.
What moved her: nothing, because no evidence was offered and her first question about who decided on the zero and whether Owen was heard first never got an answer.
What cost ground: praising her and asking for the same team, plus asking her how to handle it, because that read as flattery and as handing her your job.
Try next time: answer her opening question about who decided and whether Owen was spoken to in one honest sentence, then put a dated document on the table.
